# Motivation

## Causal bounds are often vacuous

For observational data of treatment $X$ and outcome $Y$ generated as
$$
Y = \hstar(X) + U + \xi ,
\qquad
\E{U} = \E{\xi} = 0 ,
$$
hidden confounding $U$ makes $\hstar$ generally unidentifiable.

::: {.incremental}
- *Partial identification (PI)*: bound the causal effect over all DGPs consistent with the data and assumptions $\Ppi$, i.e. the identified set $\Hpi := \set{ h^q_{\star} : q \in \Qpi }$.
- [Problem:]{.highlight} PI bounds are often too wide to inform decisions.
:::

::: {.fragment}
> Can **known data symmetries** $\sT$ — invariances $\hstar(\tau \vx) = \hstar(\vx)$, with $\sT \indep U$ by design — be repurposed as constraints that **provably sharpen** PI bounds, e.g. via post-DA data $(\tX, Y)$?
:::

## Hidden confounding leaves causal effects underdetermined

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/sem-graph.svg){fig-alt="Structural equation model with hidden confounding" width=78%}

Observational SEM with hidden confounding.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/intervention-graph.svg){fig-alt="Intervention graph for do(x)" width=78%}

The causal query asks what changes under $\doop(X=x)$.
:::
:::

## Partial identification reports a set, not a single answer

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/pi-x.svg){fig-alt="Partial-identification interval at a query point" width=88%}

At a query point, compatible DGPs produce an interval of possible effects.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/pi-metrics.svg){fig-alt="Identified-set geometry and partial-identification metrics" width=88%}

The width and position of the identified set determine how useful the bound is.
:::
:::

# Symmetry-Constrained Bounds

## Data augmentation behaves like a soft intervention

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/da-graph.svg){fig-alt="Data augmentation graph" width=78%}

Transform observations using a known symmetry.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/transformation-intervention-graph.svg){fig-alt="Soft-intervention graph induced by the transformation" width=78%}

The transformation has the semantics of a soft intervention.
:::
:::

## Point identification and PI react differently to augmentation

![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/table-point-vs-partial.svg){fig-alt="Comparison of point and partial identification under data augmentation" width=82%}

For PI, augmentation can sharpen bounds without requiring point identification.

## Symmetry yields four complementary ways to sharpen PI bounds

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="25%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/inv-pi.svg){fig-alt="Invariance-constrained identified set" width=96%}

Explicit invariance.
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/da-pi.svg){fig-alt="Post-data-augmentation identified set" width=96%}

Post-DA PI.
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/da-iv-pi.svg){fig-alt="Post-data-augmentation invariance-constrained identified set" width=96%}

Post-DA + IV.
:::
::: {.column width="25%"}
![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/pi-da-pi-intersection.svg){fig-alt="Intersection of baseline and data-augmentation identified sets" width=96%}

Robust intersection.
:::
:::

Explicit constraints prune the baseline set; DA can recenter and tighten it; their intersection remains robust under arbitrary DA.

# Experimental Results

## Simulated query sweeps: symmetry consistently tightens bounds

![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/simulation-query-sweep.svg){fig-alt="Query sweeps on simulated data" width=90%}

## Optical-device query sweeps confirm the pattern

![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/optical-query-sweep.svg){fig-alt="Query sweeps on the optical-device dataset" width=90%}

## do-MNIST: post-DA invariance gives the sharpest valid bounds

![](https://uzairakbar.github.io/symmetry4CausalBounds/do-mnist-sweep.svg){fig-alt="do-MNIST digit sweep" width=90%}

# Takeaway

## Known symmetries turn into useful causal information

::: {.incremental}
- PI is essential under hidden confounding, but its bounds can be too wide to act on.
- Symmetry constraints are an underused, principled source of extra information.
- Explicit invariance, post-DA PI, and their robust intersection all sharpen bounds while preserving validity.
:::
